counterhypotheses.claim: A dedicated lightweight embedding encoder remains Pareto-superior because generative VLM visual features are not optimized for calibrated instance/layout similarity and open-set rejection.

No learned projection is needed; deterministic pooling and prototype statistics over raw Qwen features already provide sufficient familiarity geometry and projection training only adds drift/maintenance risk.
The vision tower dominates the cost or semantic decoder consultation is required so often that decoder bypass produces little real savings.
Desktop correctness depends on global layout/background/modal context often enough that ROI token reduction creates hidden failures exceeding its compute savings.
Periodic anchors are redundant when event capture and task-triggered active sensing are correct, so anchors waste compute without measurable resilience gain.
Full screenshot history or richer scene summaries preserve cross-region dependencies that action-grounded crops systematically lose.
Text/name anchors encode semantic category similarity rather than user-specific visual identity and will increase false familiarity for visually or semantically related entities.
Feature-space temporal distance is too sensitive to rendering/crop/resolution changes and too insensitive to small but task-critical text/state changes to be a reliable decode-control signal.

Model export/mmproj coupling or quantization changes can alter the representation enough that separating visual-feature compatibility from decoder behavior is not stable across actual deployed artifacts.
Visual-seeded associative retrieval amplifies a single mistaken identity into a coherent but wrong memory context, increasing confirmation bias more than it improves task context.

The EAP core may be microsecond-fast while the real coupled path is not: seed resolution, state/hash synchronization, serialization, prompt assembly and extra context attention dominate end-to-end latency.
Preassembled associative context increases prompt tokens and distractor load, so Qwen spends more compute attending to retrieved memory than it saves through reduced search/reasoning.
Memory-guided active sensing creates self-confirming attention loops; a direct visual uncertainty policy reaches equal or better action accuracy with less architectural coupling.
Visual-temporal memory has modality-specific recency and similarity requirements that justify a specialized transient index rather than forcing all associative retrieval through shared EAP semantics.

Even provenance-bound seeds cannot guarantee fail-closed behavior when high-confidence visual misidentification is itself internally consistent; the only safe response may be deeper independent visual verification before graph propagation.
NO_DOSE_EFFECT: Qwen's native multimodal reasoning already solves the target episodes well enough that adding Frank-specific prior experience yields no reproducible net benefit across practical N.
THRESHOLD_TOO_HIGH: an experience benefit exists in principle but only after more independent episodes than Frank can realistically accumulate for the relevant entity/state class.
EARLY_OVERFIT: small-N memory improves exact recurrence while worsening state variants, novel entities or near-neighbor unknowns through false familiarity.
MEMORY_VOLUME_CONFOUND: apparent gains arise from generic extra context, cache warming or database size rather than relevant experience and disappear against matched irrelevant SHAM_N memory.
EAP_NOT_CAUSAL: at every matched N, simpler direct exact/FTS memory performs equally or better; the amount of experience matters but EAP adds no distinct causal value.
NONMONOTONIC_CONFLICT: benefit rises with N but later reverses because stale, redundant or contradictory episodes increase retrieval noise and confirmation bias.
